4 ways nonprofits overcome their biggest HR obstacles
Paylocity helps nonprofit organizations achieve long-term success through tailored tools and expertise.
Senior Marketing Manager | Customer Advocacy
While leading the Paylocity Advocacy Program, I’ve talked with clients across a wide range of organizations and heard firsthand what HR and payroll teams deal with every day.

Working at a nonprofit, you know the mission comes first. Your focus is on the communities you serve, so there's no time, or money, for HR headaches to slow you down. And let's be honest: A tight budget leaves little room for error. Without the right tools in place, fixing even a small mistake can eat into other deadlines or pile on costs you didn't see coming.
Here are four of the biggest HR challenges I hear about, and how our nonprofit clients say they’ve worked through them.
Pain point #1: Growing inefficiencies from manual and paper-based processes
Let's face it: Paper-based tasks like onboarding and performance reviews eat up your time. All that manual work adds up fast, and you feel it.

You rely on seasonal staff, volunteers, and interns to keep things moving. But with fresh faces coming through the door again and again, onboarding never really stops. And when those steps live on paper, things slip through the cracks. Work slows down, admin costs creep up, and your team spends more time chasing forms than doing the work that matters.

Lincoln Park Zoo opens in a new tab felt the strain when paper-based processes couldn't keep up with the way they actually work. Visitor numbers rise and fall with the seasons, so the team regularly onboards and trains new staff to give guests the best experience possible. Without the right setup, they were pouring time and energy into places they shouldn't have to.

Once Lincoln Park Zoo switched to Paylocity’s digital platform, they transformed every part of their HR processes and created a unified system. Genevieve Gonnigan, vice president of HR, People and Culture at Lincoln Park Zoo, shared that expanding the onboarding module sped up how quickly they could bring someone into the system.

Now, when employees log in to Paylocity, they find HR information, pay stubs, and time-off requests in one place. The zoo also uses Paylocity's Learning module to give new hires, volunteers, and current employees access to a wide range of training courses. And they lean on Paylocity’s Community tool as a central hub for communication, with dedicated groups for interns and other employees.
Pain point #2: Struggling to maintain employee morale and recognition
Recognition is easy to push aside when everyone is busy. But when employees don't feel seen for their work, morale can slip, engagement can drop, and turnover can become harder to control.

The Lawrenceville School opens in a new tab knew this challenge well. Recognition was inconsistent and rare, and it took a toll on morale across faculty, administrators, and facilities teams. Human Resources Director Kristen Oberlin noted, “We used to only have an annual Employee Appreciation, but it was a one-off event.”

A little gratitude goes a long way. When people thank their peers and employees, it builds confidence and connection across the whole organization. According to Gallup, employees who are well-recognized are 45% less likely to voluntarily leave their employer compared to employees who don’t get meaningful recognition.

Now, Kristen sees a steady stream of notifications as faculty, administrators, and facilities team members acknowledge great work and shout one another out through Paylocity’s Community and Recognition & Rewards modules.
Pain point #3: Poor internal communication

For some nonprofit HR teams, one of the trickier challenges is reaching a workforce that doesn't sit at a desk. Whether employees are outside, in a classroom, or in the warehouse, getting the right information to everyone at the right moment isn't always straightforward. Without a solid line of communication, connection can suffer, and that tends to affect both engagement and productivity.

At Humane Animal Rescue in Pittsburgh (HARP) opens in a new tab , the team relied on little more than an old SharePoint page to share their mission. They didn't have a real platform to communicate key goals or rally employees around a shared purpose.

HARP added a mobile-first approach, and suddenly, deskless employees had real-time communication and HR tools in their hands 24/7. They could check their schedule, request time off, view a paystub, or read announcements from the company without tracking down a manager.

Dan Cody, Executive Director at HARP, mentioned how employees now clock in through the Time & Labor module on the Paylocity mobile app . “In the past, we placed timeclocks in specific locations, but that felt overbearing,” Dan said. “The geofencing option in Paylocity offers more trust: once people are on site, they just punch in on the app.” By giving employees these tools, HARP delivers real flexibility, builds trust and keeps communication strong.
Pain point #4: Leaders lack access to meaningful workforce data

Plenty of organizations collect mountains of HR and payroll data but struggle to actually put it to use. At ACH Children and Family Services, employees support children and families facing difficult, sometimes tragic circumstances. That kind of demanding work can drive high turnover in key roles. Without clear insight into why employees were leaving, managers had a hard time supporting their teams. The right data could help ACH retain talented employees and spot burnout early, before they impact staffing.

Once ACH joined Paylocity, the Data Insights module gave them a way to analyze what was driving turnover, along with other HR trends. That data helped them support their team and lift morale across the board.

“If I had to highlight one great thing about Paylocity, it would be the Data Insights module,” said Laura Feghali, ACH’s HR director “The reporting gives us in HR and our team managers hard, clear data on why people are leaving their roles. It enables us to identify the things that we are doing well and the areas for improvement, whether that is offering people more targeted support or changing our compensation model. These are the things that will help us to stabilize our workforce and ensure we do a better job for families and children in need.”

After hearing from these nonprofits, one thing stands out: The organizations that treat HR as a priority are the ones moving fastest. Their edge comes from digitizing HR processes and using that foundation to strengthen the whole organization.
When you reduce the manual work of onboarding, speed up hiring, invest in community, and use data to retain employees, you build a more visible, more resilient organization.
In my experience, the best nonprofits put HR systems in place that move the work forward.
But it's always the people who inspire the mission.

He drives client success storytelling through case studies, testimonials, videos, reviews, and content that showcases how Paylocity's unified platform solves real challenges — such as unifying HR, IT, and Finance, by streamlining onboarding, improving employee engagement, and enabling strategic HR.

What Leaders Need from AI in HR Technology
Our research and our clients agree: Getting real value from AI depends on four key capabilities.
Vice President, Marketing, Revenue Growth & Operations
Innovation only matters when it creates real value in everyday use. That’s the foundation behind Paylocity’s Ignite AI, and it’s the reason we bring clients into every stage of development.
Too often, AI conversations in HR start with what the technology can do instead of what leaders actually need it to solve. That disconnect is one reason adoption falls short of expectations.

A Paylocity survey of more than 500 HR, Finance, and IT leaders shows where confidence in AI is growing — and where barriers still exist. The big picture is encouraging: 88% of HR technology decision-makers believe AI can help their teams focus on higher-value work.
But optimism alone doesn’t drive results. Our research shows that successful adoption of AI in HR depends on four key capabilities:
Prevention: Catching payroll issues early
Insight: Better visibility for workforce planning
Usability: Making AI accessible and intuitive
Security: Building trust through governance and control

I recently had the opportunity to meet several of our clients who provided direct feedback to our product and marketing teams. Their experiences confirmed that Ignite AI addresses everyday needs while sparking bolder ideas for AI’s impact.
Forty-two percent of leaders say they want AI that can flag payroll irregularities early and recommend corrections before processing — making it the most in-demand HR AI capability.

The cost of payroll and data errors is rarely limited to dollars; it also undermines employee trust. For Paylocity clients, getting ahead of those issues isn’t new. Our payroll software has long helped teams surface problems before payroll runs. With AI, that capability becomes faster, sharper, and easier to act on.

Amy Gunn, Director of Payroll for the Utah Jazz and Utah Mammoth, described the shift Ignite AI enables: “It will definitely help categorize some of the challenges we have as far as tax liability, benefits, things that are kind of buried within the payroll system that people don’t pay much attention to until there’s a problem.”

That demand reflects a shift in expectations: Business leaders no longer want HR systems that simply process transactions. They want intelligence that helps prevent operational issues long before they impact employees.

Thirty-five percent of leaders name predictive analytics and workforce planning as the top capability missing from their current HR technology. That’s a significant gap, and it points to a broader issue: Too many AI tools automate tasks without giving leaders better decision-making visibility.

One powerful use case is high-volume hiring, where speed and precision directly affect business outcomes. Ryan Zimmerman, Vice President of Human Resources for POLYWOOD, sees strong potential in using AI agents tailored to find the specialized qualifications and experience his team needs. “We do a lot of bulk recruiting where we’ll get hundreds of applications in a week,” he said. “Being able to put the specific criteria we’re looking for into the system will really help speed the process. We can spend more time sourcing, less sorting.”

But the value doesn’t stop with recruitment. As Ignite AI analyzes patterns in your workforce data, it can match people to open roles and shifts based on skills. That gives frontline managers back hours spent piecing together coverage, and it shows leaders where talent gaps are forming and how demand is shifting. The result is a workforce strategy grounded in real intelligence.

Nearly one-third of HR tech decision-makers say limited internal expertise is a major obstacle to AI adoption. That tells us two things: AI tools need to be intuitive enough to use without a technical background, and they need to deliver results that are measurable.

To see what AI is doing and how it’s working, the Ignite AI hub provides a centralized dashboard where admins can activate specific agents and access metrics about AI usage across the platform. That control gives leaders peace of mind and a better understanding of how AI is driving productivity gains.

“I definitely feel like being able to turn agents on and off, choosing what you want to utilize and testing it out, and seeing everything all in one place is a real advantage of Ignite AI.” said Robyn Klawitter, Executive Vice President of Mountainside Fitness.
When AI tools reduce friction, adoption follows more naturally. And when leaders can clearly see how those tools are being used and the value they’re delivering, confidence grows alongside adoption.
Nearly half of business leaders rank data security and privacy as the top barrier to AI adoption. That’s not a perception problem. It’s a trust problem, and it’s ours to solve.

Because Ignite AI is woven throughout our unified platform, leaders can apply AI without ever leaving the system. Consistent governance, access controls, and auditability are built into the HCM solution they already rely on for HR, payroll, and spend management.

“Using a tool that’s embedded into a trusted partner like Paylocity is the right way to use AI,” Robyn Klawitter said. “It’s the intelligent source that an executive can use and know that your partner has vetted all of the security behind it.”

At Paylocity, we don’t believe HR teams should have to choose between innovation and security. With Ignite AI, HR teams can put AI to work confidently, backed by the security, governance, and control they expect.
There’s no shortage of AI noise in the HCM market today. Leaders should be asking: Who’s actually listening to what my organization needs?

The next phase of AI in HR won’t be defined by novelty. It will be defined by trust, usability, and documented outcomes. As you evaluate where AI fits into your HR strategy, start with the needs your current tools aren’t meeting — and expect your technology provider to solve for what matters most.

Our survey made those priorities clear: proactive payroll error detection, predictive workforce insights, less friction for teams without deep AI expertise, and stronger data security. Amy, Ryan, and Robyn each pointed to Ignite AI’s ability to deliver on those needs in practical, meaningful ways.

That’s the value of co-creation. We build with clients, not just for them, so every agent is grounded in a real challenge and designed to drive measurable impact. Bring us your toughest challenges. We’re listening, and we’ll keep moving forward together.

Allison Windon leads Paylocity's marketing, demand generation, sales development, revenue operations, pre-sales, and enablement organizations, helping strengthen the brand, accelerate growth, and optimize go-to-market performance. Known for balancing creativity with analytical rigor, Allison connects brand strategy, customer engagement, and revenue performance to drive measurable business outcomes. Passionate about developing high-performing teams, Allison believes sustainable growth comes from empowering people and fostering collaboration. She earned her MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and her BA from the University of Richmond. Turn data analysis into a conversation with Ignite AI
The new Answer & Insight Agent allows you to analyze data, explore trends, and make informed decisions fast, all within the AI Assistant.

Answering everyday questions usually requires running reports, exporting spreadsheets, or waiting on someone else to look through them. When you add up all the small moments spent sifting through data, it’s one of the biggest drains on your time — and the one-off requests just keep piling up.

The Answer & Insight Agent allows you to ask just about any question and get answers in real time, pulling from your company data across the platform. You get instant insights without the overhead of reporting, writing SQL queries, or knowing the right way to analyze data. Just ask your question in natural language, and our agent gets you an answer, fast.

“What I'm seeing the most value in is the ability to analyze data with a simple conversation. Getting ready for board meetings, I used to dig through data for specific answers. Now I just say, 'How many vacancies do we have open in X department?' and get an answer in seconds.”
The agent can help with anything, from looking up a data point you need going into a meeting to doing detailed analysis across teams. Some examples include:
Performance: “What trends are we seeing in performance across the team?” and "Who’s received performance feedback but hasn't been followed up with?"
Compensation: "Are any employees outside their expected pay band?" and “What’s the average salary and distribution for customer support roles?”
Time & Labor: "What does overtime look like in hours and cost by role?" and “What teams have the highest overtime and how is it trending?”
Recruiting: "How long does it typically take to fill product design roles?" and “What’s the budget impact of hiring for the role earlier?”

Go beyond raw data with answers you can understand and act on. Get clear, organized summaries and comparisons in plain language instead of a spreadsheet to sort through. Every answer includes a link to source data if you need to dig deeper.
See important patterns called out for you. Trends and changes that might otherwise go unnoticed are front and center, helping you spot issues and opportunities faster.
Visualize data with charts and graphs. The agent finds the right way to present data, so you can understand what’s going on and get context to make effective decisions.
Go from chat to action. Take action without leaving your flow, like assigning tasks, changing an employee’s role and compensation, or initiating lifecycle events like on- or offboarding.

“Instead of running reports on things like salary trends, I can just ask, 'Tell me the average pay of our clerical staff,' and get a detailed chart without digging through the data. When a manager comes in with a quick question or someone asks in a meeting, I get an answer right away.”
Our agent isn't built around a fixed set of questions, so one question can lead to another.

Drive from broad to specific questions to get exactly what you need. Start with "Where are we seeing pockets of overtime?" Then narrow in: "Which roles or teams have the highest overtime usage?" And go one level deeper: "Are any individuals disproportionately contributing to it?"
Return to previous threads through chat history. Conversations are saved, so you can pick up an analysis from last week or keep building on a previous thread without retracing your steps.

You can trust the Answer & Insight Agent because it’s built within our proven platform and prioritizes transparency at every step — from citing its sources to measuring impact across your organization.
Each response includes clear context and links back to source data, so you can verify the output, dig deeper, and take action confidently.
It respects existing roles and access, so people only see what they're allowed to.

You control how AI works across your business. The Ignite AI Hub gives you a single dashboard to see what AI is doing and manage it with confidence. Measure its impact like how many questions it’s answered, track adoption across teams, and control who has access — all in one place.

“The piece that stood out to me is the new Ignite AI Hub. It gives us the ability to control the agents, turn them on and off, and see what they're doing and the actual value they're creating for us in time savings and task automation.”

We’re building AI into Paylocity to give you time back to focus on people and your strategy. The Answer & Insight agent is one of the best examples of that, getting you out of hunting for data and building reports and back into the driver’s seat where you can have greater impact.
To see everything this agent and our entire platform can do for your business, request a demo .

How Ignite AI Helps Recruiters Focus on the Right People, Faster
New recruiting agents automate repetitive processes, freeing you to focus on engaging candidates and partnering with hiring managers.

Hiring teams today aren’t short on candidates. They’re short on time. Every open role brings a wave of applications and resumes, and teams in high-volume environments need to move quickly without sacrificing quality.

New recruiting agents in Paylocity address these challenges by helping teams prioritize candidates who are the best match for open roles and quickly understand their qualifications. They’re embedded within existing recruiting processes, so you gain efficiency right away and stay in your flow. By making screening faster and easier, you get time back to engage candidates while staying in control of every hiring decision.
52% of decision makers are actively looking for new AI solutions in areas like recruiting to stay innovative and efficient.
- March 2026 Qualtrics Study

With hundreds of candidates applying for open roles, working through all of them takes time many teams don’t have. The Candidate Fit Agent supports both efficiency and quality by surfacing applicants for review based on the most important criteria for the role.
Set search criteria based on role requirements.
Recommended criteria: We give you a start by suggesting skills, certifications, education, and more to look for based on the job description.
Customize your search: You can tune recommended criteria or create your own to home in on the top candidates.
Compliance guardrails: Alerts flag any criteria that are vague or could potentially create compliance risk so you can adjust them proactively.
Review fit along with transparent rationale behind each assessment.
Prioritized candidate list: Applicants that match the most criteria are surfaced first along with a summary of what’s driving their fit strength.
You stay in control: While the agent makes suggestions, you own the decisions. We provide transparency into what’s driving every fit assessment, so you have the context you need.

“As a seasonal business, we do a lot of bulk recruiting — so as we’re ramping up, we get hundreds of applications a week. Having Ignite AI help accelerate the review and look for specific criteria that we are looking for will save us so much time.”

Resumes vary widely in format, length, and level of detail, creating headaches as you search for qualifying information on your top candidates. The Resume Summary Agent does the legwork by turning resumes into short summaries to triage candidates before doing a deeper review.
Get summaries that are structured and easy to understand.
